advices.diagnosis: OrderService is a classic God object: it implements order lifecycle, pricing, audit, and notification in a single class. The metrics confirm this: a high number of methods (NOM=26) and cyclomatic complexity (WMC=56) indicate a heavy workload per class, while the critical LCOM4 score of 5 shows low cohesion. The class also references four distinct internal collaborators (DCC=4), further evidencing a tangled design.

suggestions.title: Extract Audit into separate AuditLog class
suggestions.sketch: Create a new class `AuditLog` that owns the audit list and exposes methods `log`, `history`, `last_entry`, `audit_size`, and `clear_audit`. In `OrderService.__init__` replace `self._audit` with `self._audit_log = AuditLog()`. Delegate all audit-related calls to `self._audit_log`.

suggestions.title: Move notification logic to dedicated NotifierService
suggestions.sketch: Define a `NotifierService` that holds the notifier and sent counter. In `OrderService.__init__` replace `self._notifier` and `self._sent` with `self._notifier_service = NotifierService(notifier)`. Delegate `notify`, `sent_count`, and `reset_sent` to this service.

suggestions.title: Delegate pricing to PricingService
suggestions.sketch: Create a `PricingService` that owns tax rate, discounts, and related calculations. In `OrderService.__init__` replace tax and discount attributes with `self._pricing = PricingService(tax_rate, discounts)`. Delegate methods like `set_discount`, `discount_for`, `bulk_discount`, `set_tax_rate`, `apply_tax`, `total_for`, `policy_rate`, and `is_priced` to this service.

advices.risk_notes: These refactorings will change the public API of OrderService; tests and callers must be updated to use the new services or to keep thin delegation wrappers. Care must be taken to preserve shared state (e.g., next_order_id) and to avoid duplicating logic across services. Dependency injection should be used to keep the services loosely coupled.
